column3: 20 healthy males aged 21 to 31 (mean 25.1, SD 2.8), in vivo, non-participatory (relaxed) lips; upper and lower lip EMG at rest, mean RMS 19.14 and 17.57 microvolts, slope against span not significant
column4: A linear-motor servo stretches the mouth corners (interangle span) in eight steps of about 3 mm (about 24 mm in all), 3 s per step, 100 ms transitions, five blocks per subject; stiffness = change in force over change in interangle displacement between consecutive steps, evaluated over the last second of each step (N/mm); multilevel quadratic regression on the stiffness coefficients
column5: A lateral stiffness of the perioral system at the mouth corners (skin, mucosa, orbicularis oris and the buccinator and zygomatic fields together), not the transverse stiffness of the vibrating lip, so it is apparatus-effective. N/mm values are converted exactly (x1000) to N/m. The unit and origin of the regression variable Interangle_Span are not stated in the sentence that defines it; the printed step variances imply stiffness scores of about 0.03 to 0.3 N/mm, so this lane reads the span as mm of stretch from rest (an inference, not a printed statement). The female equation is quoted by this paper from Seibel and Barlow 2007 (8 females, age 25.19, SD 2.54). R-squared is the only fit statistic stored

column3: 20 healthy adults (10 male, 10 female), in vivo, non-participatory (relaxed) lips, face-referenced OroSTIFF device (no head restraint)
column4: Five interangle stretch trials per participant; stiffness coefficient = force change over a 1 mm change during the phase of elastic recoil (N/mm); multilevel null model for the mean
column5: Perioral lateral stiffness of the mouth corners, apparatus-effective; the 0.073 N/mm is the estimated mean over all trials and participants (SE 0.002 N/mm), converted exactly (x1000) to N/m. The variance split printed there puts almost all of the variability within participants
